text: NYT: "The Nest of Snakes": Warring Cartels Target Women in Mexico August 31, 2026 | 🔴 📰 The NYT gives Sinaloa's two-year internal war a horror-movie title — "The Nest of Snakes" — and makes murdered women the narrative hook. 🔍 The real story is a fragmented cartel civil war concentrated in a few states, not a nationwide collapse. 🇲🇽 Left out: Mexico's national homicides fell ~51% in July to a 12-year low. The bloodletting is localized — and it's between factions the US kingpin strategy helped splinter. • Loaded framing: "The Nest of Snakes" • A two-year Sinaloa faction war, not a countrywide surge Source

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO EXPORTS LIKE NEVER BEFORE — RECORD $81.4B IN JULY</u>

Trump's tariffs were meant to break Mexico. Instead exports hit an all-time monthly record of $81.42 billion in July — up 43.7% year-on-year, INEGI reports — with the United States still the top destination by far. Even in the middle of a tariff war, Mexico closed the January–July period with a $9.26 billion trade surplus.

✊🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO CITY EXPANDS ITS UNIVERSAL BASIC INCOME</u>

Clara Brugada handed out 20,000 new grants under Mexico City's Universal Citizen Income — 2,000 pesos every two months for residents aged 57-59, now reaching 107,000 people and headed to 150,000 this year. "Redistributing income isn't giving you a handout — it's returning part of the wealth you produced," Brugada said. The capital is piloting what could become a lifelong guaranteed income, a first in Mexico.

🕊️🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO CITY MOVES TO LEGALIZE EUTHANASIA — 86% BACK IT</u>

Days after the capital's first-ever march for the right to a dignified death, a survey found 86% of Mexico City residents support legalizing euthanasia. Mayor Clara Brugada came out in favor of advancing the debate, and the "Ley Trasciende" initiative — "my life, my death, my decision" — now heads toward consultation with affected families, doctors and specialists. A humanist reform grounded in personal autonomy.

📱🇲🇽 <u>81% OF MEXICO'S TEACHERS BACK REGULATING PHONES IN CLASS</u>

Mexico consulted 565,396 teachers — one of the largest such exercises ever — and 81% backed clear rules for phones and screens in schools, with 48% reporting cellphones wreck students' attention. "Social networks generate messages of hate and abuse that children wouldn't otherwise encounter," Sheinbaum said, as the SEP drafts national guidelines built from teachers' own voices rather than a top-down ban.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICAN FAMILIES DROWNING IN BANK DEBT AT RECORD RATES</u>

Household loan defaults just hit an all-time high — Banco de México reports overdue consumer credit reached 64.5 billion pesos, up 32.8% in real terms in a single year, with credit-card delinquency alone soaring 53%. This is the inheritance of a neoliberal banking system run by foreign megabanks charging usurious rates — precisely the model the 4T's Banco del Bienestar was built to break.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>DEA LET FENTANYL FLOOD US STREETS — THE AGENCY THAT BLAMES MEXICO</u>

For years Washington branded Mexico a "narco-state" and slapped tariffs on it in the name of fentanyl — while the DEA itself deliberately let the drug reach US streets. The US House Oversight Committee is now investigating the agency for monitoring, but not seizing, massive fentanyl shipments in New Mexico from 2023 to 2025 to build "better" prosecutions, an AP investigation revealed. The same interventionist agency that operates on Mexican soil chose bigger indictments over American lives.

🇲🇽🚗 <u>RECORD CAR SALES, TARIFFS AND ALL</u>

Mexicans bought 885,349 new light vehicles from January to July, up 5.0% and the best seven-month run since INEGI began keeping the record in 2005; July alone added 130,831 units (+3.4%). The domestic market keeps expanding even as Washington threatens the very auto sector its economy leans on.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE PAN'S SHOWCASE RUNS ON POVERTY WAGES</u>

In Querétaro, the PAN's model state, 41% of workers earn just one to two minimum wages — now the largest and fastest-growing income bracket, jumping from 293,437 to 501,440 people in a single year (+70.9%), according to INEGI's ENOE. The "competitive" state where the paychecks are smallest.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>CDMX BUILDS: 3,600 WORKS, 13,000 HOMES</u>

Mexico City will close Clara Brugada's second year with more than 3,600 public works: 13,000 new homes, 100 of 140 planned kilometers of electric transit already running, and 200,000 new streetlights along 600 km of women's safety routes. In the neighborhoods where drainage was rebuilt, flooding dropped 90% despite heavier rains.
